content.thinking:
I'm planning the design for a chunky, Warcraft-style gray wolf model with exaggerated paws and shoulders, roughly 0.85m at the shoulder, and need to be careful about unused imports causing type errors as I write the whole file in one pass.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton structure: hips as root, a spine chain running through chest and shoulders, a neck chain connecting to the head and jaw, and a tail chain extending backward from the hips, all parented correctly so the chains connect smoothly.

For the legs, I'm placing front shoulders symmetrically and defining a three-segment limb per leg (shoulder-elbow-wrist-paw) with lengths slightly longer than the straight-line distance so they naturally bend, specifying bend directions for the two inner joints to keep the canid front leg mostly straight with a backward elbow bend.

For the hind legs, I'm setting hips further back with longer three-segment limbs (hip-knee-hock-tip) whose total length is much greater than the straight distance, forcing a pronounced bend, with the knee bending forward and the hock bending backward to get the classic digitigrade dog-leg shape.

I'm having paw parts rest at ground level as flattened spheres, with leg tube radii tapering down toward the foot, and planning the body as a swept shape following the spine's catmull-rom path between hips and chest.

For the sweep, I'll just use the spine chain directly as the bone, letting the first span handle the path before the first joint, and extending the path slightly rearward for the rump. I'm defining the spine path points from hips to chest with a radius profile that's chunkier at the rump and tapering toward the withers.

For the chest radius I want it deep but not too wide, so I'm setting rx and ry with a slight downward shift to account for the belly, checking that the chest bottom clears the leg elbow height — adjusting ry and the shift until the belly sits around 0.5 for proper clearance. The hips joint and the spine chain's root joint share the same position, which works fine.

Hind legs attach to the hip root while front legs attach to the end of the spine chain. For coloring, I'm designing a mottled slate-gray coat with warm brown and cream belly tones using a toon-shaded fur edge effect, blending the base coat color into a cream underside with controlled teeth and period parameters before applying the cel-shading pass.

Adding a dark saddle marking...

Still defining leg shading...

Now for the head, I need to place it with a skull sphere scaled and jointed near the shoulders, aimed slightly forward and down. I'll just use world coordinates directly to position the head joint rather than relying on local directional words.

Working out muzzle geometry...

Adding dark nose sphere at the muzzle tip, then working out fang placement using small cone spikes on the head bone, calculating the upper and lower jaw edge positions so the teeth line up correctly at the muzzle.

Now I'm positioning the lower fangs, then placing amber almond-shaped eyes on the sides of the head with small dark pupils, plus a dark brow ridge sweeping above each eye for an alert, fierce expression.

Positioning the eyes so they sit slightly embedded in the skull with a touch of protrusion given the skull's scale factors, then moving to the ears—shaping them as pointed upright triangular extrusions positioned near the top sides of the head with a slight bevel and thickness for a sharper, pointed look.

Planning the ear tip color using a paint function that shades darker near the tip, and defining the ear outline with four points using zero smoothing to avoid sharp-corner errors. Now I'm sketching a cheek ruff fur tuft as a pointed polygon SVG shape for texture cards.

I'm figuring out how card textures get tinted by the coat color rather than using fixed greys, with paint applied at the card root so each scattered piece inherits the correct hue. I'm also planning the scatter placement across the neck ruff, chest ruff, tail, and cheek ruff surfaces, deciding roughly how many cards to use for each region and confirming the scatter function can work off a swept surface with filtering by normal direction.

Now I'm working out the skeleton: a catmull-rom neck chain running from the shoulder up through the head base, parented to the tip of a four-point spine chain that ends at the chest joint, making sure the joint array indexing gives me a valid tip reference. For the neck's swept geometry, I'm setting up radius and thickness functions so the neck tapers smoothly and lines up with the body's rounded cap at the chest.

I'm checking the head and body proportions against real wolf anatomy -- the neck end point, head position, and shoulder height need to line up so the back doesn't clip above the head. I'm recalculating the body path's y-coordinates to target a realistic withers height around 0.9, adjusting the hip and chest points accordingly.

Now I'm revising the spine path with hip, mid-body, and shoulder joint coordinates, and defining a radius function that tapers the rump, waist, and shoulders to different widths and heights along the body.

Still tuning radius function...

I'm shifting the body down slightly for a tucked-belly look and checking the chest/elbow positioning stays consistent, then working out the front leg joints—shoulder, elbow, wrist—so the limb bends naturally to reach from the shoulder anchor down to the foot target given the segment lengths available.

Adding paw and pastern segments...

Setting front leg radii slightly chunkier for that oversized Warcraft paw/wrist look, and adding muscle-bulge ellipsoids at hip and shoulder for extra bulk. Then I'm shaping the paws as flattened spheres positioned at the tip joints with wide, squashed scaling to read as big clawed feet.

Now I'm working out toe placement for each paw — four small toe bumps spread across the front edge with dark forward-pointing claw spikes beneath each one, keeping the count manageable across all four paws.

With feet done, I'm shifting to the tail — using a curved path from the base near the hindquarters down to a low hanging tip, built from a few chained segments to give it a bushy, drooping look like a wolf's tail.

Now I'm defining the taper and shading: the radius shrinks progressively toward the tip, with rounded end caps, and I'm blending the coat color from the base into a darker tone near the tail's end to mimic natural fur banding.

For the underside, I'm adding a cream-colored fur edge for the belly contrast, then scattering around 120 fur cards along the tail's curve for a textured, lean-angled look. Counting up joints across hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, tail, and legs puts me around 30 total, which seems reasonable, and I'm confirming the hips joint is created first as the root with the spine chain parented to it.

I'm assigning roles to each chain -- spine, neck, tail, leg, head, jaw -- and setting up the head joint with a forward-facing direction parented to the last neck joint, plus a jaw joint aimed slightly downward and forward from the head. I need to fix a mismatch where the neck chain's starting position doesn't line up with the chest's tip joint, so I'm adjusting the neck path's start coordinates to coincide properly, and making sure head-mounted parts explicitly reference the head bone.

Now I'm building the skull geometry as a scaled sphere positioned slightly above and forward of the head joint, then working out the head's fur coloring -- layering a mottled base coat with a paler muzzle patch toward the front of the face using a position-based edge mask along the z-axis.

I'm also adding a cream-colored underside for the jaw using a normal-based mask, plus a subtle dark stripe down the nose bridge by directly testing position and normal conditions and mixing in a darker tone where they're met.

Simplifying it instead to a small dark eyeliner sphere placed just inward of the eye, skipping the separate rim geometry since the brow already does enough work.

I'm adding a tiny white glint sphere for highlight and giving the eyes a subtle amber glow for a Warcraft-style effect, then scattering small cheek tuft cards across the sides of the skull using a position filter based on sign and depth.

For the neck and chest, I'm scattering mane cards along the body sweep, angled to flow back and down for a tufted look, and designing the tuft texture as a two-tone card tinted lighter at the tip to read as fur under the color paint.

Making a second tuft shape for variation...

I'll also scatter darker guard-hair cards along the spine to form a dorsal streak over the saddle marking.

For the mane, I'm considering sweeping frames along the back/neck but the API's return shape is uncertain, so I'll fall back to a safer scatter approach filtering by upward normal and minimum distance for spiky tufts there too. Now I'm setting up a pale chest bib with cards scattered where the normal faces forward.

Working through the neck surface scatter and shoulder/hip blob placements, figuring out bone attachments for the shoulder and thigh ellipsoids relative to the leg joints.

Now I'm setting up the leg joint chains, defining side naming conventions (left/right based on x-coordinate sign), and building the chain of points from the limb data to sweep radius profiles along each leg with the appropriate paint color.

I'm figuring out the fur coloring for legs—using a mottle coat above a level threshold and tan below, considering whether to add a darker stripe or paw markings, then settling on simpler tan/gray coloring without extra stripes for now.

Switching to texture setup, I'm deciding to keep paint resolution at 2048 to balance quality against shared texel density across all painted parts, since the atlas would get too large at 4096. For styling, I'm weighing whether to add Blizzard-style accessories like a spiked collar, but leaning toward keeping the wolf natural and unadorned rather than adding war-themed gear.

Now I'm writing a custom three-tone shading function that blends a warm highlight, base color, and cool shadow based on the light direction dot product with the surface normal, defining the light vector and threshold logic for each tone...

I'll keep the mouth closed in the rest pose rather than adding an open jaw or tongue, and give the nose a small dark glossy sphere with a tiny white highlight. For the muzzle I'm planning a swept line for the lips along the lower edge of the muzzle.

Still refining whisker dots and muzzle taper geometry...

Working out ear placement on the skull surface, scaling them smaller to match wolf proportions, then figuring the extrude parameters for thickness, bevel, and mirrored positioning with an outward tilt.

For the inner ear detail, I'm nudging the offset slightly along the thickness axis so the darker inner-ear shape sits just inside the outer ear without clipping or flickering against the front face.

Now I'm thinking about ear tip shading — darkening the ear color near the tip using a paint function based on a height threshold. I'm also considering a few extra texture details like a small faint scar across the muzzle for character, while skipping dewclaws and ear notches to keep things simpler.

Now I'm setting up position helpers and head coordinates, then starting to write the main TypeScript file importing the builder, IK limb logic, math utilities, path interpolation, and paint helpers for the creature model.

Adding more imports...

Then I'm defining the build function with a wolf-themed palette of grays, creams, and tans for the fur coat mottling.

Still defining leg and tail fur gradients...

Now I'm setting up the skeleton rig, starting with the hips joint as the root and building a spine chain using a Catmull-Rom curve through four points to define spine1 through chest.

Next I'm sweeping the body mesh along the spine with a tapered radius and coat color, then adding a neck chain extending from the chest with two segments up toward the head, sweeping it with a shrinking radius function.

I'm positioning the head joint rotated slightly upward from the neck's last joint, then adding a jaw joint, and setting up a loop to build front and rear legs symmetrically for left and right sides using root and foot anchor points.

For each front leg, since the segment lengths exceed the straight-line distance to the foot, the chain bends naturally rather than staying vertical. I'm building the leg chain with named joints for shoulder, elbow, wrist, and paw, then sweeping it with tapering radii for the limb shape.

Setting up the hind legs the same way with hip, knee, hock, and paw joints parented to the hips, using a slightly thicker radius taper. For the paws, I'm positioning small flattened spheres at each foot tip, offset slightly outward and downward to form the paw pads, with the hind paws extending further back along the z-axis than the front ones.

Still placing claws and toe geometry...

Still placing head parts...

Adding more hair layers now: a neck sweep scattering, dark guard hairs along the back and neck, and a cream chest ruff, each with its own filters, lean/bend values, and flow directions...

Working out the dark lip line and mouth placement along the lower edge of the muzzle, computing coordinates based on the muzzle's center curve and radius at the midpoint.

Still shaping jaw and teeth geometry...

Skipping tiny incisor details for now. I'm placing the nose geometry with a dark sphere and a small glossy highlight, skipping nostril detail, then moving to set up the eye components—rim, eyeball, pupil, and glint—positioning them relative to the skull center.

Working out eye socket coordinates...

Adjusting brow ridge placement...

Still refining positions...

I'm deciding whisker beard tufts and long hairs can be skipped, and considering adding a subtle dark tear-stripe sweep from eye to lip, but worried it might clip inside the muzzle surface -- leaning toward handling it via face paint instead of geometry.

Writing paint logic...

No rump blob or ribs needed, skipping belly tuck details, and I'll skip visible pads since they're hidden under the paws. For paw colors I'm just shading a base fur tone for consistency across toes, keeping total part count around 110 which stays well within budget. I'm double-checking the API types—colors accept string or Paint, scale accepts a vector array—then setting up a hit filter based on normal direction for surface detection.

I'm wiring up the surface scatter with rng, minDist, and filter options, confirming hits work as frames for card placement, and importing svg for texture generation. I'm setting up tuft textures A and B as a randomized card texture list, and verifying the contact option works correctly in chain configuration.

I'm running through my unused-import checklist to make sure everything I've referenced—shade, resolve, gradient, mottle, furEdge, rng, limb, catmull, glow, svg, paint, color types, and THREE—actually gets used. Checking the body radius taper from front to back confirms a broad chunky chest rather than a narrow wolf-like build, which fits the intended proportions.

I'm finalizing the shading vector, writing the leg root positions symmetrically, setting the jaw's aim target point, and preparing to return the completed body object.
